# CV-16 — Moving messages and multi-select

> Branch `t/maciej/cv-16-move-multiselect` · head: see the hand-back · status: built, migration waiting for its turn
> Migration: `supabase/migrations/20261016200000_chat_v2_move_messages.sql` (fixed stamp, after CV-19 in chat's queue) · applied to the local stack: no (waiting for its turn). Dry-run with `chat_move.test.sql` inside a rolled-back transaction as `supabase_admin`: 78/78. It redefines no existing function (adds two columns' worth plus three functions), so the queue ahead can't conflict with it.

## Delivered against the row

- **Server** (one migration, adds only): `chat_messages.moved_at`, `moved_by` (→ auth.users, set null), `moved_from_channel_id` (→ chat_channels, set null), each with a partial index. Helpers (server only): `chat__channel_readers(channel)` (who can read a conversation now: the same rule as `chat_can_read_channel`) and `chat__move_refile_items(ids, to)` (Catch up items of moved messages follow them for people who can read where they went; everyone else's open ones close as `closed`; "new messages" / level / added / removed lines stay put). The op `chat_op_move_messages(ids, target, confirm)` → jsonb: the person from the session; read on the source; post rights in the target; neither archived; one source; at most 100 picked (500 with chains). Own messages anywhere: when the target has readers who couldn't read the source, it answers `{status: "confirm", newly}` and moves only with `confirm`. Someone else's (any non-own row, chain replies included) only by the source's managers and admins (`chat__can_manage`), and only when nobody new would read them (refused, no confirm path). A root brings its chain; a reply moved alone leaves its chain (and drops its quote); a chain it settled reopens ("Reopened by …"); pins drop; reactions and files ride the row. Two `kind = 'event'` lines in the mover's name: `moved_out` in the source `{ids, count, to_id, to: moduo://chat_channel/…, detached}`, `moved_in` in the target `{ids, count, from_id, from: moduo://…, out_id}`. History `chat.move` on the source. Nothing pings (an UPDATE; event rows skip fan-out and the sending limit). **Undo:** the same call back (the moved ids, the source as the target) by the mover within 10 s finds the `moved_in` line and puts every row back (chains and quotes from the `detached` list), clears `moved_*`, soft-deletes both lines, re-files Catch up, and answers `undone`. **Pace:** five moves per person per 10 s (advisory lock per person, PT429).
- **Client:** `ChatRuntime.moveMessages` (`runtime.chat.supabase.ts`, `parseMoveAnswer` in `mappers.ts`), `ChatStore.moveMessages` (moved rows leave the source at once, a delta re-files them), the store drops ids named by a live `moved_out` line **or** a deleted `moved_in` line (the Undo, for readers of the target who can't read the source). The timeline hides deleted event lines. **Multi-select** in the stream (`message-stream.tsx`): ⇧↑↓ extends from the anchor, ⌘-click toggles (the first also takes the row the cursor is on), ⌘A picks every drawn message; picked rows draw as selected; Esc clears them first. While anything is picked the bottom bar's centre is the mode row Move `M` · Task `T` · Delete `⌫` with "N selected · Esc" (`bottom-bar-mode.ts`). Keymap rule 9: bare ⌫ deletes only with two or more picked, ⌘⌫ any number. ⋯ → **Move to…** (`M` on a single selected message). **Move dialog** (`dialogs/move-dialog.tsx`): "Move to…" with a filter over the conversations you're in (recent first, not this one, not archived), then, when the op asks, "Move to <name>?" with "2 people who aren't in Founders will see this" · Cancel · Move; then a "Moved to <name>" toast with Undo for 8 s. **Event lines** (`rows.tsx`): "Ola moved 2 messages to [#name]" / "You moved a message here from [#name]", the other conversation through References (a "Private item" chip for whoever can't read it). History reads "moved N messages out" / "undid a move". **Task** on a selection: one capture with the picked messages' words in order, From the first. **Delete** on a selection: one "Deleted N messages" toast with one Undo (each sent when it goes).
- **Make a note:** hidden (Notes' op and its call N19 aren't on this branch); `tests/chat-tidy.spec.ts` "Make a note" is a documented skip.

## Agent's choices (deferred to by Maciej: confirmed for building, may be reconsidered)

- **"Mentioned in" links are not written by the move** · agent (orchestrator's CV-10-fix rule: only the send/edit path writes chat `mentions` link rows) over brief §4.4 · rejected: calling `chat__link_mentions` from the op. A moved message's items show "Mentioned in" for the source conversation only.
- **"Someone else's" includes a chain's replies**: moving your own root that others replied to follows the others' rule (managers and admins, same-or-narrower only) · their words never reach new readers on someone else's confirm · rejected: letting the root's author confirm others' replies into a wider audience.
- **Undo is the same op called back** (the moved ids, the source as the target, the mover, within 10 s): it finds the move by its `moved_in` line, restores chains and quotes, soft-deletes both lines and asks no audience question · "the same op back; the two lines are soft-deleted" · rejected: a separate undo op; a reverse move that writes two more lines.
- **Undo doesn't bring pins back, and Catch up items closed for people who couldn't follow stay closed** · within 8 s both are rare; pins are dropped by the rule · rejected: storing pins for Undo.
- **A reply moved alone also drops its quote**, and a quote of a message that stays behind is dropped on anything moved; both come back on Undo · a quote pointing into another conversation would read as a broken line · rejected: keeping cross-conversation quotes. Replies left behind that quote a moved reply keep their quote (their chain stays theirs; the quote then reads as a message they may not see).
- **A non-manager can't move out of an announcement channel** (the source's move line is written in your name, and only managers post there).
- **Moving into the same conversation or from two conversations at once is refused**; a moved message keeps its time, so it lands in the target's history by when it was written.
- **Pace: five moves per person per 10 s** (PT429, the sending limit's code), counted by the `moved_out` lines you wrote (Undo isn't counted).
- **Catch up:** items about moved messages follow them for people who can read the target (an every-message / level / added / removed line stays where it is); everyone else's open ones close as `closed`.
- **Move targets are the conversations you're in** (the capture's list minus people without a DM, this one and archived ones); the server refuses the rest (e.g. an announcement channel you don't manage) with its reason.
- **The mode row shows from the first picked message** (⌘-click one → "1 selected · Esc") · so ⌘-click has visible feedback · rejected: only from two.
- **No "More ▾" yet**: its only item (Make a note) is hidden; the bar's own More appears past six actions · rejected: an empty More.
- **Delete on a selection is offered only when every picked message is yours** (greyed otherwise) · only your own messages delete · rejected: deleting the own ones silently.
- **T on a selection: one task**, the words of the picked messages in order joined by " · " (cut at 200), From the first picked message · rejected: a task per message.
- **The event line names the mover ("You" for yourself)** and the other conversation as a reference chip; the deleted (undone) lines draw nothing.
- **Picked rows stay picked when the stream loses focus** (the bar's buttons take focus); a moved or deleted message leaves the selection; switching conversation clears it.

## Gotchas (area: supabase / ui)

- DB tests share one `now()`: a pace test can't post six messages through `chat_op_send` (the sending limit counts them); write them straight in as the test's admin.
- `share_chat_message_guard` checks the announcement rule on event inserts too: an op that writes a line in someone's name must check it first or the insert fails with a less useful message.
- The store dropped ids only on `moved_out`; an Undo's soft-deleted `moved_in` must drop them too, or readers of the target who can't read the source keep the rows.

## Manual checklist (step → expect → surface)

- [ ] ⌘-click two of your messages → both highlighted; bottom bar "Move M · Task T · Delete ⌫ · 2 selected · Esc" → web
- [ ] ⇧↑ from a selected message → the range grows; ⌘A → every message; Esc → selection gone → web
- [ ] M → "Move to…" → pick a channel with people not in this one → "Move to #x?" with "N people who aren't in … will see this" → Move → "Moved to x · Undo"; both conversations show "You moved 2 messages …" → web
- [ ] Undo within 8 s → the messages are back, both lines gone → web
- [ ] As a manager, move a member's message into a private channel of a few of the same people → moves at once; into a wider one → refused with the reason → web
- [ ] Move a root with replies → the whole chain moves; move a reply alone → it leaves its chain ("N replies" drops by one) → web
- [ ] A person in the source who isn't in the target → the line "… moved 2 messages to Private item"; the messages disappear without a reload → web (two browsers)
- [ ] Bare ⌫ with one picked does nothing; with two → "Deleted 2 messages · Undo" → web
- [ ] ⋯ on a message → "Move to…" → web

## Known, left for later

- A reader of the target who can't read the source and is offline during an Undo keeps the rows on their device: `chat_sync_ids` derives `moved_away` only from `moved_out` lines; the live path (the deleted `moved_in` line) covers everyone online.
- A reply posted to a moved root inside the Undo window changes the moved set, so the Undo call then reads as a fresh move back (with lines).

## Verify before release

- Prod grants for `chat_op_move_messages` (authenticated + service_role) and the two helpers (service_role only).
- Realtime on staging: target readers get the moved rows as updates; a source reader who can't read the target loses them through the `moved_out` line within a second.
- The pace limit holds under a scripted loop (PT429 after five).
